title: Deterministic evaluation: exact match, format and rules

videos.script: From here the course stops watching the assistant and starts grading it. {{grade}} The first kind of grading needs no judgement, only a rule a program can apply. You have met it already: every exercise on this platform is marked that way. {{platform}} Twenty-four questions with their answers, and the assistant's replies to them. The comparison says sixteen are right. Two more are right in other words, and no normalisation reaches a paraphrase. {{facts}} Then rules every reply should obey: cite every sentence, cite only real sources, take every number from a source, repeat nothing personal. {{rules}} They cost nothing, so they run on every reply. On the clean questions of the set, none of them fires. On a week of customers, forty-seven replies break at least one, and one rule catches the model getting two weeks wrong. {{zero}} And every wrong answer in the set passed them. A reply that contradicts its own source has perfect form. {{form}} Rules see the form. Seeing the meaning takes something that reads. {{end}}
